title: Add records-branch writer to athena-git (retry of 20261024-033933-ta60)
summary: Retry the rejected job: add a writer in athena-git that appends opaque record files to the orphan branch athena/records using compare-and-swap, fast-forward only, bounded retry (§8.2, D111). The prior attempt was rejected only because the gate criterion had no cited commands; this attempt must run and cite the gate commands.

defaults_applied.how: The writer and its tests are Rust in athena-git.
Every new module has passing tests; cargo test and clippy are clean.
Reuse existing helpers; add no crate.
Behavior criteria name the commands to run.
Criteria check writers landing, replay, refusal and orphan history by running tests.
One focused module plus export, changelog and design note.
Doc comments cite §8.2 and D111 for an outside reader.
The tests check the outcome: the branch state after each call.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Goal: a tested, uncalled library writer; audience is the maintainer and the verifier, who run the tests.
The retry takes the original records-branch request as typed; the introspection's proposed pipeline pre-handover step is a separate job and is out of scope.
The earlier design and test list were accepted; only the evidence gap (criterion 5) and the weak contention nit need fixing.
The existing Git wrapper, temp index and commit_tree helpers in athena-git suffice; no new crate, so Cargo.toml likely stays unchanged.
Writing identical bytes at an existing path is refused (or documented as a no-op); the producer picks one and documents it.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run `cargo test -p athena-git`. A test starts two writers on threads against one repository, with different paths. Both land, both paths are on the final tip, each update is a fast-forward of the previous tip, and no commit is lost.

Run `cargo test -p athena-git`. A deterministic test makes the expected tip stale. The first update is rejected, the writer refetches and replays its files on the new tip, and the write succeeds with both the earlier and new files in the final tree. The two-thread test needs no forced contention; this test covers the reject path.

Run `cargo test -p athena-git`. Tests show that modifying, deleting or renaming an existing path is refused with an error and the tip is unchanged. A same-bytes write at an existing path is tested and its result documented.

Run `cargo test -p athena-git`. A test shows `git merge-base main athena/records` finds nothing and the first records commit has no parent. A second test shows that when every attempt is rejected, the writer returns a clear error after the bounded count.

Run `cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check` from the repository root. All pass and are clean. The producer's final report quotes each command line and its result so the verifier can cite them (D43).

A new public module in athena-git, exported from lib.rs, takes opaque bytes keyed by path. Its doc comments cite §8.2 and D111. It uses the existing Git wrapper and helpers with no new crate. No code outside athena-git calls it.

The CHANGELOG [Unreleased] section has an entry, and docs/design/records-history.md notes the writer as built. No governance file (athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflows, lint tables) and nothing under records/ is changed.

out_of_scope: Any pre-handover evidence step or other change to the job pipeline
Calling the writer from the pipeline
Pushing or publishing athena/records to a remote
Changes to governance files or records/
departures: Slightly higher cost and pass odds than reference: the code was largely accepted before, and the known rejection cause (uncited gate commands) is now explicit in a criterion.
